item.title: Tokushima Solo Travel Guide: Pilgrimage Walks, River Cycling & Mountain Solitude
item.description: There is a long tradition in Japan of travelling alone on purpose. The henro — the walking pilgrim in white who completes the Shikoku 88-temple circuit — is perhaps the most recognised form of this tradition, but the underlying impulse appears in many forms across Japanese culture: the solo hike, the midnight bridge visit, the single traveller eating at a counter watching the cook work. Tokushima, as the starting prefecture of the 88-temple circuit, has been welcoming solitary travellers for over a thousand years.
